rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm check: rule exists so a reader can't follow a pronoun/term to nothing; absent here everywhere I traced one. Walked every chunk in order. Chunk2 line14 'it names the thinking...' resolves 'it' to the just-named Willison essay same sentence; line16 'that essay' resolves to the just-linked Why Software Factories Fail same sentence. Chunk2 line14 first uses 'the send-off' before chunk3 formally bolds 'Send off' as an LO verb -- forward-shaped, but the clause self-glosses it in the same breath ('before you step away from a session, and today you step away'), so a reader never needs the later chunk to parse it; not flagged. Chunk4 line31 'The map has a far side' -- 'the map' is the compendium's own listed arc-earned exempt term (rule1 carve-out lists it by name); PASS by carve-out. Chunk4 line29 'That's the point' resolves to the room's-answers-will-differ list two clauses earlier, same chunk. Chunk6 line57 'while the read is already underway' is a forward reference to M5's activity with no same-file antecedent, but 'read' here carries its ordinary-English sense (a review of your material) and the sentence supplies the gloss inline ('scrambling for material while...') -- judged self-explanatory rather than a stranded term; noted as the closest call in the file, not filed. Chunk5 line51 'The run' is the file's first noun-use of 'run' but tracks transparently onto the already-established 'the task'/'the send-off' chain (session sent off = the run); referent resolves even though the word choice itself is a vocabulary.md §21b concern (see notes, out of this class's lane). No unresolved referent found.

grep -n 'Module 3\|Module 2\|Module 1\|that essay\|the essay' curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/run-the-first-experiment.md -> lines 14 and 16. Both name their source directly in the same sentence ('Simon Willison's [Designing agentic loops]...from Module 3/2', '[Why Software Factories Fail]...in the gap after Module 1') rather than locating by rendering position ('the opening lecture said'). Module numbers/names are the rule1 carve-out's own example of vocabulary that doesn't need re-earning, and naming a module by number is not the position-dependent shape rule2 bans. No bare positional callback found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm check: the rule exists to keep bold scarce enough that a bolded span reliably signals a named handle; diluted, readers stop trusting bold as a wayfinding cue. Located all 10 bold spans (grep -n '\*\*' over the body): line10 'A real slice you'd send off...smaller than a big epic' is the mandated check_pedagogy.md §34 task-sizing floor+ceiling callout sitting in ## Prework -- N/A by the rule's own named exception, not flagged. Lines20-23 (Scope/Walk/Fill/Send off) are the ## What You'll Learn template's one-word bolded verbs -- N/A by the rule's own named exception, not flagged. Lines63/65/67/69 (Read,/Watch,/Read,/Read (longer),) are the reading-list-menu exception's mode-word-only bolds, title left plain in each case -- N/A by the rule's own named exception, not flagged. Line29 chunk4 'Start here': '**The question, to you:** which task have you been putting off because it needs hours of babysitting?' -- a 5-word bolded rhetorical address introducing the room prompt. This is not a named law/governor/coined-term/checklist-item; it is exactly the shape rule9 names and bans outright ('Kickers/koans/quotes never bold'), independent of the per-slide count (chunk4 has only this one bold, well within the ≤1 budget -- the count is not the violation, the category is). The harm is narrow (one bold, not a monoculture) but the category match is real: this is a kicker, and kickers never bold. Same shape appears at M1's opener ('**The question (to you):**' in getting-going.md) as an apparent house pattern, but rule9 carries no carve-out for recurring templates the way it does for §34 callouts and LO bullets, and no maintainer accept-note in this file's block addresses this line.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Unbold 'The question, to you:' and let it run as plain narrative, or, if a maintainer wants to keep a recurring-kicker convention across module openers, that decision belongs in the compendium as a named carve-out (parallel to the §34 and LO-bullet ones), not as a per-file exception invented at judge time.
